title: Nori and the Little Dragon
markdown:
The Silverpine Peaks whispered peace in the gentle morning light. Nori the elf loved these quiet mornings. His little fingers, soft as new moss, would gather sparkling dewdrops from the fir needles. Each drop was a tiny perfect pearl for his cozy nook. He hummed a little elf tune, soft as a woodland breeze.

Peep-squeak, share the glow.

But today a tiny flutter, like a shy butterfly, tickled Nori’s tummy. It was a worry about his shimmering moon-moss, found yesterday. It glowed with a soft silvery light. What if someone saw it? What if they wanted it? His chest felt a little wobbly, and his fingers felt a bit less steady. His hands wanted to hide. His mind felt a little cloudy.

A little walk would help settle his tummy. Nori skipped along the soft pine-needle path. Deeper into the fir grove he went, where the needles chimed like tiny bells in the light breeze. Then he heard it. A little peep, and a long sighing sound, like a sleepy balloon. Nori tiptoed closer, peeking around a big mossy stone. There, nestled in the ferns, was a small dragon. Its scales were soft sunset colours: gentle orange, rosy pink, and sleepy lavender. Its wings looked like velvet, tucked softly by its sides.

The little dragon looked up, its honey-gold eyes meeting Nori’s. It opened its mouth, and out came a tiny high-pitched sound, like a surprised little mouse.

“Peep-squeak!” it whimpered, then covered its snout with its paws, looking shy.

Nori’s heart felt warm. He knew what it was like for a sound to not come out right. He remembered his own little elf voice, which used to squeak when he was very surprised.

“Hello,” Nori said, his voice like rustling leaves. “That was a very interesting hello. It sounded very friendly.”

The dragon peeked out, a blush of pink spreading on its snout, like the first hint of dawn. “It’s… it’s not a roar,” the dragon mumbled, its voice a whispery squeak. “It’s supposed to be a roar, like my Uncle Ignis. But it always comes out like a startled robin. Or a very surprised tea kettle. My name is Flicker.”

Nori smiled, a warm smile that reached his eyes. “I’m Nori. And your peep-squeak hello is very friendly. It makes me want to smile.”

Flicker seemed to relax, his shoulders slumping a little less. Nori thought of his shimmering moon-moss. It glowed softly, a gentle light. He thought about showing it to Flicker. But his worry came back, a little stronger. What if Flicker did not understand how special it was? What if he thought it was just ordinary moss? Nori took a small step back, his eyes darting to his little pouch. He thought about just going home, keeping his treasures safe and sound. He really wanted to turn back, to his quiet nook.

Then Flicker let out another soft sigh, like a puff of warm air. He looked at his own little paws. Nori watched him, and his worry began to melt like frost in the sun. He remembered his own little squeaky voice, and how kind it felt when others did not make him feel silly. Sharing his moon-moss felt more important than keeping it all to himself.

Nori took a deep breath. He reached into his pouch. He pulled out a piece of the softly glowing moon-moss. Its silver light was a gentle beacon.

“This,” Nori said, his voice clear and steady, “is for you. It glows in the dark. It’s very special. It makes lovely patterns on the wall when the moon is out.”

He held it out, feeling a little flutter of his old worry, a tiny pang of giving up something so precious. He felt the soft cool texture of the moss in his fingers, smelled its faint clean scent, and saw its quiet gentle glow. Then he let it go.

Flicker gasped, a soft sound like wind chimes. He reached out a hesitant claw, smooth like a polished pebble, and gently touched the moss. A tiny happy sound escaped him. “Peep-squeak-chuckle!” it went, a delightful little noise. Nori giggled, a light bubbly sound. Flicker carefully took the moss in his warm claws, his whole face beaming.

They did not hurry the next step. Nori sat on the mossy stone and let Flicker watch one silver pattern bloom on the fern. A fir needle chimed. Flicker’s velvet wings stayed tucked.

Together, Nori and Flicker walked side-by-side toward Nori’s cozy home in the Silverpine Peaks. The moon-moss cast a soft silvery glow between them, a little lantern lighting their path. The worry that had fluttered in Nori’s tummy was gone. The firs kept their chime. The pouch, a little lighter, still smelled of moon-moss.

Peep-squeak, share the glow. The glow, now, had two.
characters: Nori (young elf of the Silverpine Peaks), Flicker (sunset-scaled little dragon)
author: StoryGen Community
